_comment: The stamped LINKED tier: how many matched translation units actually reach the
PC port's binary. This is a STAMP, not a live counter, and it cannot be anything
else from main: port/tools/linkage.py reads build/port/walk_window.map, which only
exists after an MSVC build of the port, and CI on main has no such build.
BEFORE STAMPING, LOOK FOR A BUILD THAT ALREADY EXISTS. Every port lane carries its
own build tree, so a current walk_window.map is usually already on disk:
ls -la */build/port/walk_window.map
across the port worktrees, newest first, then run the tool against that root. The
first version of this file was stamped off a five-day-old branch while a map from
the night before sat unread one directory away, and published 26.5% when the real
figure was 34.5%. A stale stamp is still a real measurement, just of the wrong run.
To refresh: run `python port/tools/linkage.py [root]` and update the numbers below
together with branch, commit and measuredAt. Never move the count without also
moving the provenance fields - tools/tiers.py drops a stamp missing any of them,
which is the intended behaviour for a number nobody can trace.
basis records what the figure is a measurement OF. The port branches are not merged,
so this is the best single lane rather than a combined total. All seven live lanes,
lk5 3819. Overlapping but not identical seats, so the merged figure is higher and
the published number stays a floor.
LINKED grows when matched TUs become reachable in the port's linked call graph.
Actor methods and free functions both count. Enrollment alone does not increase
the count when the release build still dead-strips the unreachable object.
basis: integration branch port/link100 at its pushed tip 428b68ad5, measured against that tip's own battery build walk_window.map (C:/tmp/l1-int, gate INT15: tree clean, reconfigure with CONFIGURE DEPS 250/5, battery ALL GREEN at floor 10170 with all 51 level and 36 scene rows, nine proofs green including the opening-cutscene gate, the loopback session and the stage seat proof, a captured run showing the game-init arms, the frame cross-check at 0 disagreements and the ROM's archive table 13/13 resident), and confirmed by the hosted-runner port-linkage workflow on every push of port/** and every pull request into the shipping branch (a GitHub Windows machine with no cartridge; the shipping branch takes landings only through such pull requests, with the count required by a branch rule). +46 over the previous stamp of 10170, +183 over the 2026-09-08 morning's 10033, +1095 over the 2026-08-30 stamp of 9121. Since the 10170 stamp, seven gated lanes: the two wireless link-state readers (+2) and the ROM's own wireless bring-up up to WM_Init registering its reply handler (+12; nineteen DS globals hosted at ROM span; the transport opens on the ROM's own channel claim; nothing is asked of the host ARM7 yet), the ROM's archive-mount table hosted and LoadArchive answering from it because every archive is resident on the host (+8; the table's twenty-six ROM strings mounted by the generator), twenty-four object-field pointer-to-member rows in three gates (+24; one row refused on a wrong-overlay crossing in the decomp), the comms fan-out running the ROM's narrow bodies and extending them for sixteen players (0), and the other maintainer's review corrections on the game-init arms (0). Gated rungs since the last stamp: 10170 -> 10180 -> 10216. Known and pre-existing, found by bisect this day: the port's default rollback netcode does not carry the VS match-end state across a rewind, so a four-player match can desync on the frame the match is won; the fix is gated separately. Staged behind the next gate: the ROM's own NitroFS init reading the cartridge header through the shared-memory mirror (+11).
